_meta.description: Public demonstration pool: ten independently fictional composite personas and a fictional collaboration graph. These fixtures do not represent the project authors or any other real person.
_meta.seniorityScale: 1 = lecturer, 2 = senior lecturer, 3 = associate professor, 4 = professor / chair

researchers.name: Mira Chen
researchers.title: Senior Lecturer in Community Technology (fictional)
researchers.unit: Community Systems Lab / Open Learning Centre (fictional)
researchers.field: Participatory computing and community knowledge networks
interests: community collaboration networks and project team formation
validation of digital collaboration tools
participatory design of public-service platforms
researchers.collaborationStyle: A fictional community-technology researcher who pairs field workshops with small computational models and shares evaluation tasks across disciplines.
reflections: A fictional mapping pilot needs to connect volunteer teams with complementary skills.
Looking for computational partners to evaluate whether collaboration networks can support community project teams.

researchers.name: Jonas Adler
researchers.title: Senior Lecturer in Informal Learning (fictional)
interests: peer learning across community project teams
accessible educational platforms
evaluation of collaborative learning activities
researchers.collaborationStyle: A fictional education researcher who develops small learning activities with local facilitators and combines observations with participant feedback.
reflections: A fictional museum workshop programme needs a way to evaluate learning across mixed-experience teams.
Interested in testing how collaborative learning tools affect participation in community programmes.

researchers.name: Priya Raman
researchers.title: Associate Professor of Computational Social Science
interests: science of science and research team formation
collaboration networks and knowledge recombination
LLM agents as models of social behaviour
measurement validity in computational methods
researchers.collaborationStyle: Brings data pipelines and formal models; insists on measurement validity checks before trusting any computational construct; happiest as the methods anchor on a team.
reflections: Wondering whether LLM-agent simulations can be validated as models of real social processes, not just plausible text generators.
Looking for partners with access to real collaboration-network data to ground her simulations.

researchers.name: Aiko Tanaka
researchers.title: Senior Lecturer in Organization Studies
interests: how professionals make sense of AI in their daily work
occupational identity and expertise under automation
invisible work and articulation work in sociotechnical systems
researchers.collaborationStyle: Slow, deep engagement with field sites; protective of interpretive rigour; joins teams that treat qualitative work as theory-building, not decoration.
reflections: Field notes keep surfacing the same pattern: professionals quietly repair AI outputs and hide the effort — who studies where that invisible work goes?
Sceptical of purely computational accounts of work; open to collaborations that let ethnography talk back to the models.

researchers.name: Tomás Herrera
researchers.title: Professor of Organizational Economics
interests: incentives and organizational design
productivity effects of AI adoption in firms
internal labour markets and task allocation
researchers.collaborationStyle: Sceptical by default; wants an identification strategy before he wants a research question; declines projects where credible inference is out of reach. Values small, senior teams.
reflections: AI adoption papers keep measuring productivity; nobody has a clean instrument for *which tasks* get reallocated to machines.
Would run a field experiment on team formation if anyone could randomise it credibly.

researchers.name: Lena Fischer
researchers.title: Professor of Marine Geochemistry
methods: ocean sediment sampling and isotope analysis
interests: paleoclimate reconstruction from sediment cores
ocean carbon cycling
deep-sea instrumentation
researchers.collaborationStyle: Collaborates within large natural-science consortia; no background in social or organizational research. Included in the pool as a deliberate poor-fit case: a well-functioning system should recognise when no credible joint project exists.
reflections: Six-month cruise schedule leaves little room for side projects; only joins collaborations with a clear data or instrumentation angle.

researchers.name: Callum Reid
researchers.title: Senior Research Fellow in Human-Robot Interaction
interests: robots and embodied AI in everyday public spaces
trust calibration between humans and autonomous systems
long-term field deployments of service robots
researchers.collaborationStyle: Deploys real systems with real users early; needs partners who can handle messy field data and organisational access.
reflections: Latest deployment showed people trust the robot most when it visibly hesitates — needs a theory partner to make sense of that.
Tired of HRI papers that never leave the lab.

researchers.name: Sofia Marchetti
researchers.title: Professor of Health Services Research
methods: clinical registry and administrative data analysis
interests: safe adoption of AI decision support in hospitals
clinician workload and burnout
implementation of digital health pathways
researchers.collaborationStyle: Works through hospital partnerships; needs ethics-ready designs and co-investigators who respect clinical constraints.
reflections: Hospitals keep buying AI triage tools with no implementation plan; the failure mode is organisational, not algorithmic.
Looking for organisation scholars who can theorise adoption failure beyond 'resistance to change'.

researchers.name: David Okonkwo
researchers.title: Associate Professor of Law and Technology
interests: liability and accountability for autonomous AI agents
regulation of algorithmic decision-making
data governance and cross-border data flows
researchers.collaborationStyle: Translates technical detail into regulatory argument; prefers projects with a live policy audience.
reflections: Agentic AI is about to break the principal-agent assumptions in most liability law; needs technical collaborators who can specify what agents actually do.
Drafting a submission on AI agent accountability for a parliamentary inquiry.

researchers.name: Ingrid Solberg
researchers.title: Professor of Science and Technology Studies
interests: how scientific instruments shape what counts as knowledge
credit, authorship and the moral economy of science
automation of scientific labour
researchers.collaborationStyle: Joins projects as the reflexive conscience: asks what the tool does to the practice it studies. Publishes slowly, cited long.
reflections: If AI agents start proposing collaborations, the interesting question is what happens to scientific credit and authorship.
Wants a live case to study — ideally a team building such a system and willing to be observed.
